faq.heading: Frequently asked questions about digital maturity
faq.a1: Digital maturity is the extent to which a company uses digital tools and processes to streamline operations, decision-making and customer experience. It is measured along several axes: processes, systems, data, infrastructure, security and governance.
faq.q2: How does the assessment on digitalizuj.to work?
faq.a2: You fill in an adaptive questionnaire (15 questions for a quick screening or 43–49 for the comprehensive assessment). Based on your answers you get a DII-Compatible score, Operational Readiness score, AI & Automation Readiness, Technical Debt & Risk Index and Business Impact Potential with savings estimated in hours, person-days and EUR.
faq.q3: What is the DII (Digital Intensity Index)?
faq.a3: The DII is the official indicator of enterprise digital intensity collected by Eurostat across the EU. It scores the adoption of 12 digital technologies and enables comparison against the EU benchmark.
faq.a4: No. All data is processed locally in your browser. No answers, results or identifying information are sent to any server.
faq.q5: How long does the assessment take?
faq.a5: The indicative quiz takes 5–7 minutes (15 questions). The comprehensive assessment takes 15–20 minutes (43–49 questions with adaptive branching).
faq.q6: What is the mandatory e-invoicing requirement from 1 January 2027?
faq.a6: From 1 January 2027 Slovakia introduces mandatory B2B electronic invoicing via the Peppol network under the EN 16931 standard. The test checks whether your invoicing is ready for the transition and counts unpreparedness into the risk index.
faq.q7: Who is affected by NIS2 and Act No. 366/2024 Coll.?
faq.a7: The NIS2 directive, transposed in Slovakia by Cybersecurity Act No. 366/2024 Coll., extends obligations to thousands of mid-sized companies in energy, transport, manufacturing, healthcare and digital services. The test tracks NIS2 unpreparedness among its monitored risk factors.

methodology.heading: About the methodology
methodology.body: The assessment rests on two layers: the DII-Compatible Layer (benchmarked against the EU Digital Intensity Index) and the Operational Digital Readiness Model (actual operational digital maturity). Questions are adaptive — they adjust to your answers (Adaptive DAP model). Every score is auditable and can be decomposed back to its inputs.
methodology.intro: digitalizuj.to is a free online digital maturity test for small and medium-sized enterprises. In 5 minutes it measures your company’s level of digitalisation, compares it with the EU and SK benchmark (Eurostat DII 2025) and estimates annual savings from automation — anonymously and with no sign-up.
